stops.title: Your shortcuts, all in one place
stops.body: The Library holds every shortcut as a tile. Click a tile to run it, right-click for more, and drag files onto it to run it on them. Ctrl+N makes a new one.

stops.title: Build a shortcut from steps
stops.body: Search the list of steps, add one, then fill in the blanks. A blank can use the result of an earlier step, the clipboard, or ask you each time. Select a shortcut and press Ctrl+E.

stops.title: Run it and see what happened
stops.body: Press F5 in the editor to try a shortcut. The results drawer shows each step as it finishes, so you can see what worked and why something did not.

stops.title: Quick Run from anywhere
stops.body: Press Win+Alt+Space in any app, type a shortcut name or alias, and press Enter. Ctrl+K opens the same search inside the main window. You can change the keys in Settings.

stops.title: In the tray, and at your pointer
stops.body: Automation Portal keeps running in the tray when you close the window. Right-click the icon for your pinned shortcuts, or press Ctrl+Alt+P for the Quick Panel at your mouse pointer.

stops.title: Let things start themselves
stops.body: An automation runs a shortcut when something happens: a time, a new file, a power change and more. Add conditions, choose to be asked first, and test it safely. Making new automations is a Pro feature.

stops.title: Type a short code, get the text
stops.body: A snippet swaps a short code such as ;sig for longer text, with placeholders for the date, the clipboard and more. Turn it on with the switch and it works in any app.

stops.title: Do it once, and let it repeat
stops.body: Choose New shortcut, then Record a new shortcut. Automation Portal writes down your clicks and typing as steps you can edit. Press Ctrl+Alt+Esc to stop a macro recording.

stops.title: Start from a ready-made shortcut
stops.body: The Gallery has shortcuts for everyday jobs. Preview one, add it to your Library, and change it however you like. Nothing is added until you say so.

stops.title: A record of every run, and Undo
stops.body: Run History shows each run step by step. If a run changed your files, Undo file changes shows the list first, then puts them back. Nothing is overwritten.

stops.title: AI steps, on your terms
stops.body: Describe a shortcut in words, or add steps that summarise and rewrite. Use Portal AI Host on this PC, Windows on-device AI, or your own account. You always get a draft you can edit.

stops.title: From Explorer and the command line
stops.body: In the website version, right-click files in Explorer or use Send to to run a shortcut on them. In a terminal, ap run "Name" runs one and returns the result.

stops.title: Make it look the way you like
stops.body: In Settings, Appearance sets the accent colour, window background, corners, density, text size, motion and tile look. Reset appearance puts everything back.
